newsitem.title: FRANCE: French refiners say remain open to talks.
newsitem.headline: French refiners say remain open to talks.

text.p: Total and Shell France said on Friday they were open to resume talks on a restructuring of refineries in the Mediterrenean.
Spokeswomen for the two companies were reacting to a statement by Industry Minister Franck Borotra that such discussions between Shell, Total and BP had been blocked.
"I do not think that they are blocked. We are ready to resume talks after the Shell announcement, which we welcome," said a spokeswoman at Total.
At Shell France, a spokeswoman said the company had been forced to take a unilateral decision to scale down capacity.

"We have not been able to find a solution in discussions with the other companies and this has led us to announce our decision last week. We are waiting for approval from the Industry Ministry," she said.
But she said "the door remains open" to further talks with the other companies.
There was no immediate reaction at BP France.
The refineries around Berre lake near Marseille are: Shell's Berre, Lavera owned by BP, Fos by Exxon and the Total-operated La Med refinery.

Shell last week announced it planned to cut its capacity at Berre and said it had sought formal approval to reduce crude throughput to 3.5 million tonnes per year from 6.5 million tonnes and shut one of its two catcrackers.
In an interview with Les Echos on Friday, Borotra said the Shell initiative was "a minimum".
